words.gloss: for the one with a beautiful forehead

literal: In the black pupil, O image, you go away; for the one with a beautiful forehead whom I desire, there is no space.
translation: O image in the pupil of my eye, please leave! There is no room here for my beloved of the beautiful forehead whom I adore.
modern: என் கண்ணின் கருமணியில் இருக்கும் பாவையே! நீ வெளியேறிவிடு. நான் விரும்பும் அழகிய நெற்றியை உடைய என் காதலி அமர்வதற்கு இங்கே இடமில்லை.
explanation: The lover playfully addresses the tiny reflection or pupil-image (pāvāi) in his own eye. He asks this image to leave (pōthāy) because he wants his beloved, who has a beautiful forehead (tirunutal), to enter and reside in his eyes. Since the pupil is already occupied by the reflection, he claims there is no room (illai iṭam) for her. This poetic conceit beautifully illustrates how the lover wishes to keep his beloved constantly in his sight and heart.
